sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203], with operating income growing faster at 12.3% [F204] and net income at 14.7% [F205].

The window is not a straight line: growth stepped up to 17.5% in FY2021 [D189] and 15.8% in FY2022 [D238], then fell back to 6.8% in FY2023 [D287] and 5.0% in FY2024 [D336] before recovering to 8.2% in FY2025 [D385] and 10.1% in FY2026 [D434].
The FY2021 step came from comparable sales up 16%, with non-foods and e-commerce particularly strong, plus gasoline price and volume effects [P56][P54].

The FY2022 peak was driven by comparable sales up 14% and a $14.8 billion increase in warehouse ancillary and other businesses, strongest in gasoline, business centers and travel, with inflation explicitly cited [P42].
The FY2023 slowdown followed as comparable sales growth eased to 3% and non-foods sales declined [P32].
The U.S. segment supplied 72.5% of FY2026 revenue [D670] and 7.2pp of the 10.1% growth [D672][D434], with Other International adding 1.6pp [D679] and Canada 1.3pp [D686].
FY2026 net sales rose $27.3 billion, or 10%, primarily on comparable sales up 8% (5% average ticket, 3% frequency) plus 25 net new warehouses [P14].
By product, Food and Sundries contributed 2.6pp of FY2026 growth [D560] and Non-Foods 2.2pp [D576], while warehouse ancillary and other businesses jumped 19.9% for 3.7pp [D600][D601].
Membership fees grew 11.0% to $5.9 billion [D664][S78], driven by new sign-ups, fee increases and Executive upgrades, with renewal rates of 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide [P13].
Operating income grew 12.5% against revenue growth of 10.1% in FY2026 [D435][D434], an incremental operating margin of 4.7% [D457], so profit grew faster than revenue.
Diluted EPS grew 14.0% against net income growth of 13.9% [D438][D436], with the diluted share count essentially flat at 444.4 million [X100][D452].
Operating margin reached 3.9% in FY2026 [F32], its window high [D691] and above the 3.4% median [D692], versus a low of 3.1% in FY2019 [D690].
The FY2026 margin rose 0.1pp [D447], with SG&A adding 0.1pp [D460] and cost of revenue flat [D459]; SG&A fell to 9.0% of revenue [D414].
SG&A as a percentage of net sales decreased 10 basis points, though excluding gasoline price inflation it rose one basis point, and foreign currency increased SG&A by $126 [P9].
Gross margin percentage decreased three basis points, but excluding gasoline price inflation it was 11.22%, up 10 basis points, helped by IEEPA tariff refunds of three basis points [P12].
Net margin reached 3.0% [F52], above the 2.6% window median [D695], with the effective tax rate at 24.7% [D420] versus 32.8% in FY2017 [D8].
Operating cash flow reached $15.8 billion in FY2026 [F82], 1.71x net income [D421], and free cash flow was $9.4 billion [F102], 1.02x net income [D422] against a 0.99x window median [D701].
The FY2026 operating cash flow increase was primarily due to higher operating income and reduced net investment in merchandise inventories from faster turns and improved supplier payment terms [P6].
Free cash flow margin was 3.1% [D418], above the 2.8% median [D698], while capex of $6.4 billion [F92] was 2.1% of revenue [D417] and 2.41x D&A [D423].
Investing cash outflow rose to $6.4 billion from $5.3 billion, primarily capital expenditures [P5][F112][F111].
Net cash reached $15.1 billion in FY2026 [D427], 5.0% of revenue [D428], the 100th percentile against retail peers (n=6) whose median is -4.4% [D715][D716].
Cash and investments grew 39.4% to $21.3 billion [D453][D425] while total debt rose 6.5% to $6.2 billion [D454][D426], and the current ratio was 1.06x [F182] against a 1.02x median [D704].
Financing outflow of $3.4 billion covered dividends, buybacks, debt repayment and withholding taxes [P4][F122].
Buybacks plus dividends of $3.3 billion were 35.2% of free cash flow [D429][D430], and the diluted share count fell 0.1% [D452], so capital return has not shrunk the share base.
Return on average equity was 28.4% [D433], the 60th percentile against retail peers (n=5) whose median is 24.0% [D719][D720].

No red-flag candidates were supplied in the pack, so severity and persistence cannot be ranked; the conditions screened were margin compression, cash conversion, leverage and dilution, and none of those triggered on the cited figures.

The one structural soft spot is margin level rather than direction: operating margin of 3.9% [F32] sits at the 17th percentile against retail peers (n=6) whose median is 5.0% [D709][D710], and net margin of 3.0% [F52] is also 17th percentile against a 3.5% median [D711][D712].

That gap reflects the membership-fee model rather than deterioration, since the margin has risen from 3.1% in FY2019 [D690] to its window high [D691], but it leaves little room if merchandise costs outrun sales.

Cash conversion is the second item to watch: free cash flow/net income of 1.02x [D422] is above the 0.83x peer median [D718] but below the 1.58x window high [D700], and FY2022 showed it can fall to 0.60x [D699].

Operating margin: a FY2027 print below the 3.9% FY2026 level [F32] would reverse the trend of the last three years, while holding at or above it confirms the operating leverage; it appears in the FY2027 10-K.
Free cash flow/net income: a reading below the 0.99x window median [D701] would signal working-capital or capex pressure, given FY2026's 1.02x [D422]; it appears in the FY2027 cash flow statement.
Membership fee growth: a print below the 11.0% FY2026 rate [D664] would test the fee-increase and Executive-upgrade driver cited in the filing [P13]; it appears in the FY2027 10-K.
Net cash: a fall below the $9.5 billion FY2025 level [D378] from FY2026's $15.1 billion [D427] would mark a shift in capital allocation; it appears in the FY2027 balance sheet.
